# Steal An Egg Wiki — Full Site Summary

Steal An Egg Wiki is an independent fan-made guide to the Roblox experience Steal An Egg by and Collect Rare Pets. The exact Place ID is 107778070777162. This identifier distinguishes the covered experience from similarly named Roblox games.

The core gameplay loop is: steal an egg, escape, return it to the player's pen, place and hatch the egg, receive a pet, earn income, buy upgrades, train speed and attempt better eggs. Eggs, pets and progression have separate topic pages so every major search intent has one canonical destination.

Divine Eggs at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/divine-eggs/ explains the Divine rarity path without claiming that every source egg has a Divine object label. It separates verified source-to-pet links from unknown egg labels, odds, and spawn rules.

Cosmic Egg at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/cosmic-egg/ is the focused Cosmic Egg and Cosmic Biome entity page. It covers verified source-to-pet coverage, how-to-get guidance, rarity context and hatch expectations without inventing nest coordinates, odds or a finished roster.

Rarest Pets at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/rarest-pets/ lists pets confirmed in the highest named rarity tier without inventing an absolute rarity ranking or treating rarity as a pet-income ranking.

The Steal An Egg Calculator at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/calculator/ performs local browser calculations from player-entered cash, income, upgrade-cost, session, and run-time values. It does not read Roblox servers or assume hidden game formulas.

The homepage at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/ is the central game entity and topic hub. Supporting pages cover eggs, rare eggs, a browser-based spawn predictor, best-egg rankings, Stag Egg, Parasite Egg, rarities, pets, Ice Dragon, Koi, Dodo, best-pet rankings, a beginner guide, progression, speed and treadmill training, codes, updates, the Sakura Event, the Monster Update and the What Happened status page.

The Spawn Predictor at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/spawn-predictor/ calculates a local countdown from the last observed spawn and custom interval entered by the player. It does not connect to a Roblox server and does not claim an official spawn schedule.

Best Eggs at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/best-eggs/ and Best Pets at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/best-pets/ provide verification-first tier frameworks. Rankings remain unfilled until original gameplay confirms names, rarity, source, income, difficulty and progression value.

The Sakura Event guide at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/updates/sakura-event/ organizes Cherry Blossom, Great Bloom, Crane and Sakura Incubator queries. Unknown mechanics, costs, timers, rewards, odds and dates remain marked for in-game verification.

The Monster Update guide at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/updates/monster-update/ covers Titan Temple, Hungry Monster infected-egg feeding, Monster Egg store content, Monster Chest rewards and Mutant Shark. Exact odds and incomes without local captures stay labeled.

What Happened to Steal An Egg at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/updates/what-happened-to-steal-an-egg/ answers removal, deletion and return queries with dated listing checks. Exact Roblox game-specific enforcement wording remains marked when not officially confirmed.

Rarities at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/rarities/ explains the Common-to-Divine rarity order and how egg rarity differs from pet rarity without inventing hatch percentages.

Stag Egg at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/stag-egg/ is the Secret Stag entity page for Cherry Blossom location, how-to-get guidance, rarity context and hatch expectations.

Ice Dragon at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/ice-dragon/, Koi at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/koi/, and Dodo at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/dodo/ are focused pet entity pages. They cover the individual source, rarity, income, and progression questions while marking unsupported fields as pending verification.

Divine Unicorn at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/unicorn/ is the focused entity page for the Unicorn search intent. It separates the documented Cosmic Egg source path, Divine rarity, and reported standard-income baseline from changeable live-game conditions, hatch odds, and route requirements.

Divine Fusion Guide at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/divine-fusion/ is the focused mechanic page for Divine Fusion queries. It explains how to check current access, requirements, interface behavior, and outcomes without presenting an unverified shrine location, recipe, cost, success rate, or reward table as fact.

Hacks & Glitches at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/hacks-glitches/ covers reported, patched and unverified Steal An Egg hack or glitch claims. It emphasizes safer progression alternatives and does not provide scripts, executors, bypass steps or credential collection.

Parasite Egg at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/eggs/parasite-egg/ is a focused egg entity page. It distinguishes the egg-specific source, rarity, hatch, and value questions from the broader Monster Update overview, and does not claim an unverified Monster Chest relationship.

Divine Kitsune at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/kitsune/ is the pet page for Kitsune searches. It keeps the documented Divine label separate from source, income, hatch chance, and route details that are not consistently documented.

Nightflame at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/nightflame/ is the pet page for Divine Nightflame. It uses the Titan Temple Monster Update lead without turning income, odds, or an official egg-object title into a fixed claim.

Titan Temple Guide at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/titan-temple/ covers the late Monster Update biome: where it sits, how access is checked, and which reported eggs and pets belong to the area. It does not replace the Monster Update overview or the Nightflame pet page.

Enchanted Forest at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/updates/enchanted-forest/ covers the announced future biome, release status, and checks for access, eggs, and pets once gameplay is live.

Dr. Scramble Boss at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/dr-scramble-boss/ focuses on finding and completing the boss encounter, with fight and reward details tied to current gameplay rather than fixed undocumented rates.

Mutations at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/mutations/ is the broad mutation hub. The Mutation Consumable guide at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/mutation-consumable/ covers item use and Fractured context. Scrambled Mutation at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/mutations/scrambled/ covers the named result and its separate application route.

Red Panda at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/red-panda/ covers one Cherry Blossom pet. Skeleton Horse at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/skeleton-horse/ and World Burner at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/world-burner/ cover two Angels & Demons pet leads. All three pages keep live panel values separate from community-reported figures.

Game Revenue at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/how-much-does-steal-an-egg-make/ states that no verified official revenue figure is published for Steal An Egg. Public popularity metrics such as visits and player counts do not equal revenue. The page identifies the experience as Steal An Egg by and Collect Rare Pets, Place ID 107778070777162, and it does not invent dollar or Robux totals.

Free Pets at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/free-pets/ explains normal egg-to-pet gameplay: steal an egg, return it to the base, and hatch a pet without treating that route as a Robux pet purchase. It invents no free-pet codes and stays consistent with the codes page. Only verified acquisition routes are stated.

Data accuracy is a core editorial rule. Exact spawn rates, prices, pet income, rarity, speed requirements, treadmill levels, mutation odds, codes and update dates are not published without verification. Empty database fields are labeled “To be verified” instead of being filled with estimates.

Steal An Egg Wiki is not affiliated with Roblox Corporation or and Collect Rare Pets. All related trademarks belong to their respective owners.

Enchanted Mutation at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/mutations/enchanted/ owns the named mutation and tightly related Enchanted Essence intent. Current corroborated coverage connects Wisp access, the Butterfly Net, Butterfly Bloom and the tree shrine. A reported butterfly recipe is attributed; conflicting income multipliers, stacking formulas and event timers are not fixed values. No separate Essence page is created.

Enchanted Tree at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/guide/enchanted-tree/ owns location, unlock, access, interior features and door troubleshooting. It publishes only current supported route information, separates Wisp quest progress from returning Wisp, and does not freeze disputed quest counts or Speed thresholds. It is separate from the dated Enchanted Forest update overview and the full mutation guide.

Spirit Panda at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/spirit-panda/ owns the pet and close Spirit Panda Egg source variants. Current public rosters associate the pet with Enchanted Forest and report Cosmic rarity. Exact egg-object names, hatch odds, income, spawn schedules and availability end dates are not stated without reliable evidence; predicted earnings are excluded.

Royal Skywhale at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/royal-skywhale/ owns the specific pet and close egg-source variants. Current public rosters report Enchanted Forest and Divine rarity; current fusion coverage also names it as a Guardian input. Exact hatch odds, income, input quantities, consumption and inheritance rules are not published as settled facts.

Celestial Sunlion at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/celestial-sunlion/ owns the specific pet and close egg-source variants. Current public rosters report Enchanted Forest and Eternal rarity, while walkthroughs also use the name for the forest guardian. The page separates those roles and keeps unknown income, source-object labels, odds and disputed fusion quantities unset.

Spirit World Guardian at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/spirit-world-guardian/ owns the fusion pet, source and progression intent. Current coverage connects it with the Enchanted Tree fusion room and reports Divine rarity. Conflicting recipes, player counts, consumption rules, mutation inheritance and modified income examples do not establish fixed requirements or a standard base income. Only supported current evidence is stated, with uncertainty made explicit.

Mutation Calculator at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/calculator/mutation/ calculates final income, increase amount and increase percentage from user-entered base income and a custom multiplier. A second custom multiplier uses the same baseline for comparison. No fixed verified mutation presets, stacking rules or application-probability model are assumed. Example inputs are mathematical illustrations, not game values.

Spectral Mutation at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/mutations/spectral/ covers the Halloween Phantom Express, Souls and Soul Extractor consumable route. Recent coverage reports a reduction from 1,000 to 500 Souls, a 25% application chance and a community-reported 2.75× income effect. These are attributed, changeable observations rather than fixed official values; check the current panel. Consumable exchange and successful application are separate.

Starry Fox at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/pets/starry-fox/ covers the Enchanted Forest pet source and reported Secret rarity. Exact official egg-object labels, standard base income, hatch odds, spawn timers, access thresholds and availability end dates remain unset. The pet route is kept separate from Wisp and tree progression, and modified income examples are not treated as base stats.

Nitro Mutation at https://steal-an-egg.github.io/mutations/nitro/ covers the documented racing-era Trophy exchange and egg application. The reported 475-Trophy price is historical event context, not proof of a currently open shop. Public coverage reports a 10% application chance, while conflicting income estimates are not fixed as a multiplier. Saved consumables and current acquisition availability need separate checks.
